book.title: Frankenstein · Chapter 6 — The Letter from Home
book.author: Mary Shelley, Frankenstein (1818), Chapter 6

cast.name: Victor
cast.canonical: a thin young man, round head, neat short dark bowl-cut hair, small round glasses, plain shirt
cast.anchor: small round glasses and a plain work apron

cast.name: Clerval
cast.canonical: a cheerful young man who always wears a black top hat

cast.name: Elizabeth
cast.canonical: a gentle young woman with braided hair

cast.name: Justine
cast.canonical: a sweet frank-faced young servant girl with a white cap

cast.name: William
cast.canonical: a small cherubic boy with dimples wearing a little sailor cap

cast.name: Waldman
cast.canonical: a kindly older professor with spectacles

cast.name: Krempe
cast.anchor: a blunt scowl and old wig

panels.scene: a dim sickroom, Victor propped weakly in bed while Clerval hands him a folded letter; morning light from a window; empty wall across the top

teen.narration: STILL WEAK FROM MONTHS OF FEVER, VICTOR IS HANDED A LETTER FROM HOME — FROM HIS COUSIN AND BELOVED, ELIZABETH. HER WORDS WILL PULL HIM BACK TO LIFE.

panels.scene: a young woman at a writing desk by a tall window, quill in hand, worried tender expression, soft backlight; the upper-right is bright empty window

teen.narration: HER LETTER IS ALL WORRY AND LOVE — BEGGING FOR JUST ONE WORD THAT HE IS ALIVE.
teen.quote: You have been ill, very ill... Get well—and return to us. You will find a happy, cheerful home and friends who love you dearly.

panels.scene: a sweeping view of a blue alpine lake ringed by snow-capped mountains, a peaceful lakeside villa below, wide open sky across the top

teen.narration: SHE PAINTS THE HOME THAT WAITS FOR HIM — GENEVA, UNCHANGED, SERENE, AND SAFE.
teen.quote: The blue lake and snow-clad mountains—they never change; and I think our placid home and our contented hearts are regulated by the same immutable laws.

panels.scene: a gentle young servant girl in a white cap, frank-hearted and smiling shyly, standing in a simple sunlit kitchen doorway; empty wall upper-right

teen.narration: SHE TELLS OF JUSTINE, THE FAMILY’S BELOVED SERVANT GIRL, RAISED ALMOST AS A DAUGHTER AND CHERISHED BY ALL.
teen.quote: if you were in an ill humour, one glance from Justine could dissipate it... Justine was the most grateful little creature in the world

panels.scene: a shadowy flashback montage: small coffins and a grieving, cold-faced mother turning away from the lonely girl; muted and sorrowful; dark empty sky at top
panels.composition: flashback montage, small figures, low key

teen.narration: BUT JUSTINE’S LIFE HAS BEEN A STRING OF CRUELTIES: A MOTHER WHO BLAMED HER, AND SIBLINGS LOST ONE AFTER ANOTHER.
teen.quote: One by one, her brothers and sister died; and her mother, with the exception of her neglected daughter, was left childless.

panels.scene: a somber winter deathbed, a frail old woman passing away as the girl keeps quiet vigil; a cold window with bare branches; empty upper-left

teen.narration: THIS LAST WINTER HER REPENTANT MOTHER DIED, AND JUSTINE RETURNED AT LAST TO THE ONLY FAMILY THAT EVER LOVED HER.
teen.quote: she is now at peace for ever

panels.scene: a sweet cherubic little boy with curling hair and dimples laughing in a garden, a tiny girl beside him; bright empty sky at top
panels.composition: sweet close portrait, warm and bright

teen.narration: AND SHE GUSHES ABOUT LITTLE WILLIAM, THE BABY OF THE FAMILY — A HAPPY DETAIL THAT WILL LATER BREAK YOUR HEART.
teen.quote: he is very tall of his age, with sweet laughing blue eyes, dark eyelashes, and curling hair. When he smiles, two little dimples appear on each cheek, which are rosy with health.

panels.scene: an extreme close-up of a delicate hand signing a letter with a quill, an anxious eye reflected in a window beyond; empty lower-left desk surface
panels.composition: extreme close-up on hand and quill

teen.narration: SHE SIGNS OFF STILL AFRAID FOR HIM, PLEADING FOR A REPLY.
teen.quote: Write, dearest Victor,—one line—one word will be a blessing to us.

panels.scene: Victor at a desk writing a reply, weak but calmer, over-the-shoulder view of the page; empty upper-right wall

teen.narration: HER LETTER REVIVES HIM. HE WRITES BACK AT ONCE, AND FROM THAT DAY HIS RECOVERY FINALLY TAKES HOLD.

panels.scene: Victor flinching away from glass chemical instruments on a shelf while Clerval quietly carries the apparatus out of the room; empty upper-right

teen.narration: BUT ONE DEEP SCAR REMAINS: HE NOW DREADS SCIENCE ITSELF. THE MERE SIGHT OF A LAB TOOL SICKENS HIM.
teen.quote: I had conceived a violent antipathy even to the name of natural philosophy.

panels.scene: a bright lecture study where a kindly spectacled professor warmly praises Victor, who forces a pained smile; empty wall at top

teen.narration: KIND PROFESSOR WALDMAN PRAISES HIS GENIUS — NEVER GUESSING THAT EVERY KIND WORD IS AGONY.
teen.quote: M. Waldman inflicted torture when he praised, with kindness and warmth, the astonishing progress I had made... He meant to please, and he tormented me.

panels.scene: a squat gruff professor throwing up his hands in blunt astonishment while Clerval stares; comic and exaggerated; empty upper-left

teen.narration: GRUFF KREMPE IS BLUNTER STILL, LOUDLY BRAGGING THAT HIS STUDENT HAS BEATEN THEM ALL.

panels.scene: Victor and Clerval bent over exotic books by warm lamplight, dreamy eastern imagery of gardens and sun floating around them; empty dark top

teen.narration: TO FLEE HIS MEMORIES, VICTOR JOINS CLERVAL IN THE POETRY OF THE EAST, AND FINDS IT SOOTHING.
teen.quote: life appears to consist in a warm sun and a garden of roses,—in the smiles and frowns of a fair enemy, and the fire that consumes your own heart.

panels.scene: a glorious spring panorama, two friends rambling a path through blossoming hedgerows and green fields under a serene sky, tiny in the vast landscape

teen.narration: COME SPRING, THE TWO TAKE A WALKING TOUR, AND VICTOR’S OLD JOY IN NATURE FLOODS BACK.
teen.quote: A serene sky and verdant fields filled me with ecstasy... The present season was indeed divine; the flowers of spring bloomed in the hedges

panels.scene: a warm moment on the path, Clerval laughing and gesturing as he lifts Victor's spirits, sunlight through leaves; empty lower-right foreground

teen.narration: IT IS CLERVAL’S GENTLENESS, NOT MEDICINE, THAT TRULY HEALS HIM.
teen.quote: Excellent friend! how sincerely you did love me, and endeavour to elevate my mind until it was on a level with your own.

panels.scene: a lively village square on a Sunday, peasants dancing, Victor striding along beaming with happiness; bright open sky at top

teen.narration: HE COMES HOME ALMOST HAPPY — NEVER GUESSING THIS IS THE LAST CALM BEFORE THE STORM HIS OWN HANDS BEGAN.
teen.quote: My own spirits were high, and I bounded along with feelings of unbridled joy and hilarity.
